report:
PASS for the exact bounded/continuous scope of proposal132: arbitrary-cardinality algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero fields, smooth integral projective X of positive dimension, and an actual nef rational L with its canonical trivial reference. This does not establish the unchanged original P16.5 or an equation theory on the larger unbounded nef E¹ space.

I independently opened [BJ v4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4) and read the pertinent complete statement/proof units for the numerical cone, envelope reduction, energy pairing and mixed measures, including §§3.2, 4.1–4.2, Lemmas 5.9/5.17, Theorem 5.20 with Lemma 5.22, and Definitions/Theorems/Propositions 7.6–7.19. Theorem 5.20 expressly concludes nef, whereas Lemma 5.17 expressly assumes ample. Remark 7.16 expressly distinguishes the larger floor-defined space. I also read the pertinent continuous-metric construction in [BE v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.01016v3), including Theorems 7.14/8.4, Definition 8.7 and the multilinear extension following it. The supplied whole G0 body is used only within its granted ample domain, at the actual bundle L+εH. Smooth integral X satisfies that body's geometric hypotheses. No documentary identifier supplies a mathematical premise.

The bounded-domain inclusion is valid for every genuine bounded θ-psh input: u is (θ+h)-psh, and constant bounds give finite ample energy. Its restriction to Xlin therefore belongs to the published ambient Ẽ¹. Consequently the published pairing and measure constructions apply before any perturbation limit. Their PL compatibility gives the original model intersections, including ord_F(𝓧₀); their positivity gives positive Radon measures, and their constant-test identity gives the raw mass θⁿ. The reference pairing at zero vanishes, and constant translation changes energy by cθⁿ while leaving curvature products unchanged. The operator is already characterized on the original carrier, so subsequent ample limits identify it rather than define an inverse lift. Its construction and characterization contain no H, establishing auxiliary-ample independence.

The decreasing-continuity applications have the required endpoints and domains. A tail of a bounded decreasing net has the lower bound supplied by its bounded limit and the upper bound supplied by its first tail member. All factors lie in E¹(θ+h). This also applies to every qε for ε≤1. For arbitrary fixed numerical coefficients, Theorem 7.14 and Proposition 7.19(iv) genuinely allow decreasing nets in one common ample finite-energy cone. The signed coefficients cause no gap: write (α,v)=(α+aω,v)−(aω,0), choosing a so that α+aω≥ω. Expansion expresses each coefficient measure as a fixed finite signed sum of positive products with fixed intersection masses, giving a uniform total-variation bound. Thus continuous-test convergence is justified, not merely PL-test convergence. Each energy coefficient likewise has a finite limit. Multiplication by positive powers of ε therefore makes the corresponding terms vanish. Proposition 7.19(v) is used only for ambient Ẽ¹ tests.

Nef envelope membership follows directly: constant competitors bound the supremum, its usc regularization is θ-psh by the envelope property, and that regularization remains below continuous f, hence is a competitor. The nef envelope property can additionally be reconstructed from the granted ample envelope property, Lemma 5.9 and PSH2. For qε, cone inclusion gives monotonicity as ε decreases; the common constant bounds ensure generic finiteness of the limit. Varying-class decreasing closure makes that limit θ-psh. The competitor inequalities then identify it with Pθf. This proves membership and the energy/operator limits without assuming continuity of Pθf.

The uniform-convergence reduction is correct. With errors ej=4^(−j), the shifted subsequence vj=uj+3ej satisfies vj−v(j+1)≥3(ej−e(j+1))−ej−e(j+1)=ej>0 and decreases to u. The constant shifts leave measures unchanged and change energy by 3ejθⁿ. For mixed tuples, choose one subsequence controlling the maximum of the finitely many errors and apply the same shift componentwise. Every subsequence has such a further subsequence. Each continuous-test pairing is consequently sequentially continuous on the sup-norm metric domain, hence continuous there; arbitrary uniformly convergent nets follow. No metrizability of Xᵃⁿ or monotone theorem for arbitrary Borel nets is used. Envelope order and translation give the stated Lipschitz estimate.

Both supporting inequalities and both derivative signs check. In the ample case, q≤q+s(f−q)≤f implies that the intervening envelope is q. The granted derivative in the continuous direction f−q gives orthogonality. Energy concavity along the genuine segment from q to r=Pωg gives the tangent inequality; positivity and r≤g then give Fω(g)−Fω(f)≤∫(g−f)Mω(q). Applying this once at f and once at f+tg produces the two bounds. Passing ε↓0 at fixed t is legitimate by the previously established limits. For t>0 the quotient lies between the perturbed-base integral and the base integral; for t<0 their order reverses. Envelope Lipschitz continuity and bounded-product sup-norm continuity make both bounds tend to ∫gMθ(Pθf). Thus both derivatives exist with the claimed raw formula. Concavity also passes through the pointwise limits of the ample functionals. When θⁿ=0, positivity makes the top-degree measure zero, and energy monotonicity between constant bounds makes the bounded top-degree energy zero; no probability normalization occurs.

Harmless clarifications: Ẽ¹ membership means restriction to Xlin, while the bounded inputs themselves remain actual functions on Xᵃⁿ. Remark 7.23 states compatibility for ample inputs; its application to continuous nef inputs should explicitly use the actual-metric decomposition (L,u)=(L+H,u)−(H,0), followed by the published multilinear extension for continuous dpsh metrics. Both terms are in the ample domain, and their expansion agrees termwise with the BJ product. This is a finite multilinear application of the existing construction. The θ appearing in the competitor family in the printed proof of Lemma 5.17 should read ω. These clarifications require no substantial repair.
